- **The `tps-mail` capability: a bob agent answers TPS mail (#200).** `bob run <name>` runs an inbox consumer that answers each accepted mail with ONE turn in a FRESH session through the agent's launcher — never in the warm session, so a reply draws only on what that turn read. Accepting happens before any session exists: the inner signed envelope is verified against the sender's key as registered in the agent's Flair (Ed25519 over RFC 8785 bytes — the CLI's own check, ported, pinned by envelopes the CLI's `signEnvelope` produced), its signed `from` is bound to the record's `from` and to `X-TPS-Sender`, the envelope must be addressed to the agent, and the verified id must be on the required, non-empty, exact-match `senders:` allow-list; anything else moves to `refused/` with a counted reason and is never answered (`X-TPS-Trust` is not consulted). New mail is processed one at a time, oldest first by filename. The turn runs through `bob launch` with `BOB_MAIL_TURN=1` and the verified fields on stdin (never argv), under a wall-clock timeout that kills the launcher; the task contract in the system prompt is the capability's fixed frame (the never-do list and the reply rule), and the mail body — control, bidi, zero-width and tag characters stripped, length-bounded — sits only in the user message, in a block delimited by per-turn random markers. A mail turn holds ONLY a reviewed allowlist — `flair_search`, `flair_get`, `flair_write`, where the role allows them — and every other tool from any role, position grant or capability is dropped (for an agent bound to a position the narrowing applies to the grant's resolved tools exactly as to a role's) (no file tool, including builder-local's anchored `read_lines`/`edit_lines`/`insert_after`/`write_file`, no shell, no Discord); keeping `flair_write` means allow-listing a sender also permits mail-influenced memory writes (documented). The reply is the turn's final message under the compaction contract's finality rule (tool-only, empty → no reply; error-ended → a failed turn), capped at `maxReplyChars`, sent with `tps mail send <sender> --stdin --reply-to <messageId>` (fixed argv, body on stdin, `TPS_AGENT_ID` = the agent's own id), then a DURABLE `replied/<messageId>` marker (temp + fsync + rename + directory fsync; any failure, a directory fsync included, leaves the mail un-acked, and bob tries to take the marker back), then the move to `cur/`. An EXISTING marker is trusted — to ack a re-delivery or to refuse a collision — only after bob has fsynced the `replied/` directory itself, so a marker left behind by a failed sync and a failed removal is never acked on; a failed sync is retried, after a restart too. A `replied/` directory that cannot be fsynced gets its own error and fails `bob doctor`, which inspects the `replied/` entry itself without following it (a broken symlink or a non-directory fails). The marker records the verified sender and a digest of the signed envelope (outer signature normalized to the verified bytes): a re-delivery of the same envelope acks with no second reply; a marker is used only after schema validation of every field bob writes (sender, digest, inboundId equal to this inbound, outcome, at), which cannot prove who wrote the file; an existing marker causes an `id-collision` refusal only after a successful read and schema validation show a different envelope, and pending-settlement or pending-reply state this run holds for the id causes it too; a marker read error is retried, and a marker that fails schema validation HOLDS the mail in `held/` with its `.reason` written before the move (counted, and shown by doctor). A marker that cannot be written leaves the mail un-acked and uncounted in `new/`, where the retry writes the marker without resending. A failed turn, an unreachable Flair, a failed send or a failed marker is counted, logged, and left in `new/` for a retry with backoff (a composed reply is resent without a second turn). Delivery is at-least-once: a second reply, threaded to the same `messageId`, is possible when the runtime dies before a durable marker or when the CLI timed out or exited non-zero after it may already have delivered; a record that cannot be checked (e.g. a non-finite number canonicalization cannot encode) is refused, since retry is reserved for the key service. The launcher runs as its own process group, which is reaped as soon as the launcher process EXITS or the turn is aborted — not when its output closes. Once the launcher has exited and process-group reaping is exhausted, if result collection is still pending, Bob starts a result timer set to fire 250 ms later (subject to event-loop delay). If reaping is exhausted and that timer fires before the output closes, Bob ends result collection and then closes its output ends. If the timer fired before the turn timeout or shutdown, the launcher exited zero, and the turn is still active, the normal result parser uses the bytes already read. The bytes read at timer expiry decide the outcome: a complete result stands without rerunning the turn, while an incomplete result fails as `no-result`; bytes written later are not used. Under those conditions, result collection does not wait for the turn timeout. Reaping sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace, probing on a nominal 50 ms poll interval (with no hard bound under event-loop delay) for up to the grace plus a reap limit, after which remaining members are logged with the group id and counted (`reapExhausted`); parser use after that exhaustion is also logged with the group id and counted (`resultCollectedAfterReapExhausted`); signals go only to a group a probe has just found. The turn gets the consumer pid at spawn and, before reading its input, requires it to be its parent; after that it ends when that pid is gone or it is reparented. The consumer lock is taken over only from a DEAD pid, never by age, through an exclusive claim keyed on that pid, so racing restarts end with exactly one holder; an empty lock, an empty claim, or a claim naming a dead process fails the start naming that file and when it is safe to remove it. Mail turns never enter the warm session's turn admission (#147) and are not reflected in presence: they run concurrently in their own process, and the roster holds one activity. `bob doctor` FAILS on a `channels.tps_mail` nothing honours, an invalid `tps-mail:` block (an empty `senders:` also refuses to load), a missing Flair identity, a missing inbox, a host that is not a TPS delivery target (#134), or a missing `tps`/signing key, and reports refused counts per reason, turn failures and reply failures. Allow-listing a sender grants it the agent's read scope (documented). STATED LIMITS: the reply needs a `tps` that accepts `--stdin` and `--reply-to`, which `tps` 0.7.0 does not — until it does every reply fails closed (counted, retried); `tps` 0.7.0 also cannot read the PEM key `bob onboard` writes. (`test/capabilities/tps-mail/`, `test/shell/mail-consumer.test.ts`, `test/shell/mail-turn.test.ts`, `test/shell/doctor.test.ts`, `test/shell/persistent.test.ts`, `test/shell/launch.test.ts`, `test/shell/positions-195.test.ts`)
